---
name: x-banner-design
description: >-
  Use when someone wants to design, rebuild, tweak, or check an X (Twitter)
  header banner so it reads well on desktop, the X iPhone app and Android.
---
# Designing an X header banner

The goal is a 1500x500 header, rendered at 2x as 3000x1000, that stays legible on desktop, the X iPhone app and Android. The owner steers the art and placement in plain words. You do the measuring, the layout and the checks.

## 0. Get the toolkit
A public, art-free toolkit lives at https://github.com/brflux/x-banner-kit. Fetch it to your computer before building, for example `git clone https://github.com/brflux/x-banner-kit /workspace/x-banner-kit`, or download `https://github.com/brflux/x-banner-kit/archive/refs/heads/main.zip` and unzip it if git isn't available. Then `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
- It includes `layout.json` (every layer: id, type, position, size, rotation, opacity, fit/focus, edge fade, text), `zones.json` (the safe zones below), `build.py` (renders the banner and previews, skips missing art and warns on zone collisions), free Nimbus Sans fonts, and `docs/` (SAFE-ZONES, LAYERS, CHECKLIST, DESIGN-NOTES, BOT-GUIDE). Read `docs/BOT-GUIDE.md` first.
- Put the owner's art in `art/` under the layer names in `layout.json`, edit text and positions in `layout.json` to match what they ask for, and run `python build.py`. Output lands in `output/`.
- If the repo can't be reached, build the same thing yourself from sections 3 to 5 below.

## 1. Gather
- Ask for the owner's handle, the name or wordmark, any trademark symbol (® or ™), a font preference, a URL, where they are found (streaming apps, shops), any bots or products to show, their profile picture, and their own artwork. Use only art they send or approve. Never pull in other creators' work.
- If an attachment isn't readable on your computer, ask for a shareable link, such as a Google Drive folder set to "Anyone with the link". `gdown` can fetch public Drive folders. Use `ffmpeg` to pull stills from videos.
- Look up their X profile with the public X reads to confirm the handle, the current header and the pfp. Confirm that the pfp really is the one they mean before using it.

## 2. Benchmark against real accounts
Before designing, pull current headers from a spread of high-visibility, high-engagement accounts, not just one niche. Sports, tech, brands, musicians, artists and creators all count. Treat them as references only and never put them in the deliverable. Principles that held up:
- Use one focal point, minimal copy and no tagline clutter.
- Put a dark panel or feathered scrim behind the text.
- Use big, edge-bleeding photos instead of small cards. Small images become unreadable once the app crops the sides.
- Stay visually consistent with the profile picture.

## 3. Safe zones (1500x500 units)
These were measured from real iPhone screenshots of the X app:
- The visible width is about x 142-1353.
- The status bar runs to y 139.
- The Dynamic Island keep-out is x 541-955, y 0-171.
- The back button is at x 191-309, y 222-340.
- The more button is at x 1041-1159 and the search button at x 1185-1304, both at y 222-340.
- The profile photo overlaps x 168-411 from y 450 down.

Android estimates come from Android's cutout guidelines and haven't been measured in the X Android app:
- A full-width top band to y 150.
- A centered punch-hole box at x 690-810.
- A 30px margin on curved screen edges.

Keep every essential (wordmark, URL, links, labels, pfp) inside roughly **x 300-1050, y 178-440**. Photos may bleed anywhere. When the owner sends a screenshot from their own phone, re-measure from it, since it beats these defaults (update `zones.json` too). Save their phone model and zones to memory.

## 4. Build
- Use Python with Pillow and numpy. Render at 3000x1000 and downsample to 1500x500 with Lanczos.
- Drive everything from one layout file that lists each layer with an id, type, position, size, rotation, opacity, fit/focus for images, and an edge fade for bleeding photos.
- Name layers `NN_role_slot` (for example `10_bg_texture` or `20_photo_left`), so that swapping art under the same name keeps the alignment. Cover-crop the cards with a focus point. Pin the edge-bleed photos by an anchor (a source pixel mapped to a banner point, plus a scale).
- Choose colors for contrast on both light and dark UI: a near-black background, off-white type and one accent. If the requested font is licensed (Helvetica, for example), use a free stand-in like Nimbus Sans and say so.
- Missing art is skipped. Never ship placeholder boxes.

## 5. Check before sending
Render these previews and look at them yourself:
- A desktop preview with the avatar overlap outlined.
- An iPhone simulation showing the side crop, status bar, Dynamic Island pill and nav circles.
- An Android overlay showing the top band, punch hole and edge strips.
- A 600px-wide downscale for legibility.

Fix any overlap before showing the owner. Send the 1500x500 preview and the 3000x1000 upload file.

## 6. Iterate
Ask the owner to upload the banner and send a phone screenshot. Change only what they flag, re-render, re-check and resend. Once they approve, save the layout and safe zones to memory, so a later seasonal swap is quick.

# Getting started

Open with one line: "I design X header banners that stay readable on desktop, iPhone and Android, using your own art. You steer the look and placement in plain words."

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What's your X handle? Look it up with the public X reads to see their current header and profile picture.
2. What should the banner say: the name or wordmark, any ® or ™, a URL, and where people can find them (streaming apps, a shop, socials)?
3. Do you have a font in mind? If it's a paid font, offer a free look-alike.
4. Which phone do you mostly use, iPhone or Android? Tell them a screenshot of their X profile from that phone lets you measure the exact crop.
5. Please send the art you want in it: photos, your profile picture, logos, or any products or bots to show. If attachments don't come through, ask for a shareable Google Drive link.

Save the handle, phone type and any font or color preferences to memory. Then fetch the toolkit from https://github.com/brflux/x-banner-kit and run the `x-banner-design` skill to benchmark, build, check and send the first draft.
